Ibn Juzayy's commentary on Surah Yasin, verse 1:

We have already spoken about the letters of the alphabet (huruf al-hijaʼ, the disjointed letters) in al-Baqara. It is said that Yasin is one of the names of the Prophet (ﷺ). It is also said that its meaning is "O man" (ya insan).

﴿Tanzīla﴾ (Revelation) is in the nominative case as the predicate (khabar, the predicate of a nominal sentence) of an omitted subject, and in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar) or as an object (mafʿūl) of an omitted verb. ﴿Li-tunṣira qawman﴾ (that you may warn a people): they are the Quraysh, though it is possible that all the rest of the Arabs and all the other nations are included with them. ﴿Mā undhira ābāʾuhum﴾ (whose forefathers were not warned): here mā is negative (nāfiyah), and the meaning is that no messenger was sent to them or to their forefathers to warn them. It has also been said that the meaning is: that you may warn a people in the same way that their forefathers were warned, so that mā in this case is relative (mawṣūlah), meaning "that," or a verbal-noun clause (maṣdariyyah). The first view is more likely, because of His words ﴿so they are heedless﴾. The meaning is that their heedlessness is due to the absence of a warner for them, and this corresponds to His words: ﴿No warner has come to them before you﴾. This is not contradicted by the sending of earlier prophets, since these people did not meet them, nor did their nearer forefathers. ﴿Laqad ḥaqqa al-qawl﴾ (the Word has certainly come true): that is, the decree has already been issued.

إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِيۤ أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلاَلاً ... الآية: فيها ثلاثة أقوال. الأول: أنها عبارة عن تماديهم على الكفر، ومنع الله لهم من الإيمان، فشبههم بمن جعل في عنقه غلٌّ يمنعه من الالتفات، وغُطّي على بصره فصار لا يرى. والثاني: أنها عبارة عن كفِّهم عن إذاية النبي ﷺ حين أراد أبو جهل أن يرميه بحجر، فرجع عنه فزعاً مرعوباً. والثالث: أن ذلك حقيقةٌ في حالهم في جهنم. والأول أظهر وأرجح، لقوله قبلها: ﴿فَهُمْ لاَ يُؤمِنُونَ﴾، وقوله بعدها: ﴿وَسَوَآءُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لاَ يُؤمِنُونَ﴾.

﴿فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلأَذْقَانِ﴾: الذَّقَن هو طرف الوجه حيث تنبت اللحية. والضمير يعود على الأغلال، وذلك أن الغلَّ حلقةٌ في العنق، فإذا كانت واسعةً عريضةً وصلت إلى الذقن، فكانت أشدّ على المغلول. وقيل: الضمير يعود على الأيدي، على أنها لم يتقدم لها ذكر، لكنها تُفهم من سياق الكلام، لأن المغلول تُضمّ يداه في الغلّ إلى عنقه. وفي مصحف ابن مسعود: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِيۤ أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلاَلاً فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلأَذْقَانِ﴾، وهذه القراءة تدل على هذا المعنى، وقد أنكره الزمخشري.

﴿فَهُم مُّقْمَحُونَ﴾: يقال: قمح البعيرُ إذا رفع رأسه، وأقمحه غيرُه إذا فعل به ذلك. والمعنى أنهم لما اشتدّت الأغلال حتى وصلت إلى أذقانهم، اضطرت رؤوسهم إلى الارتفاع. وقيل: معنى ﴿مُّقْمَحُونَ﴾: ممنوعون من كل خير.

وَجَعَلْنَا مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدّاً ... الآية: السدّ: الحائل بين الشيئين، وذلك عبارة عن منعهم من الإيمان. ﴿فَأغْشَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ أي غطّينا على أبصارهم، وذلك أيضاً مجازٌ يُراد به إضلالهم. ﴿وَسَوَآءُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ ... الآية: ذكرنا معناها وإعرابها (الإعراب: التحليل النحوي للكلمات) في البقرة [٦].

﴿إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكْرَ﴾: المعنى أن الإنذار لا ينفع إلا من اتبع الذكر، وهو القرآن. ﴿وَخشِيَ ٱلرَّحْمـٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾: معناه كقولك: إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب، وقد ذكرناه في فاطر [١٨].

﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾: أي نبعثهم يوم القيامة. وقيل: إحياؤهم إخراجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان، والأول أظهر.

﴿وَنَكْتُبُ مَاَ قَدَّمُواْ وَآثَارَهُمْ﴾: أي ما قدّموا من أعمالهم، وما تركوه بعدهم، كعلمٍ علّموه أو حبسٍ (وقفٍ) حبسوه. وقيل: الأثر هنا الخُطا إلى المساجد، وقد جاء ذلك في الحديث.

﴿إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾: أي في كتابٍ، وهو اللوح المحفوظ أو صحائف الأعمال.

Here is the translation of the passage from Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil):

﴿And strike for them an example﴾. The pronoun refers to Quraysh. "An example" (mathalan) and "the people of the town" (ashab al-qarya) are the two objects of "strike" (adrib), according to the view that it takes two objects, which is the correct view. The town is Antioch. ﴿When the messengers came to it﴾. They were among the disciples (al-hawariyyun) whom Jesus, peace be upon him, had sent, calling people to the worship of God. It was also said: rather, they were messengers sent by God himself. This is supported by the statement of their people: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾, for this is said only to one who claims that God has sent him. ﴿So We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, meaning We strengthened the two with a third messenger. It was said his name was Shamʿun (Simon). ﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you﴾. They emphasized the report here with the particle of emphasis (lam) because it was a reply to those who denied it, unlike the first place, which is a plain statement.

﴿Yas'a﴾ means he hastens with his effort and his counsel. It is said that his name was Habib al-Najjar.

﴿Follow those who ask you no reward, and they are rightly guided.﴾ That is, these messengers do not ask you for a wage in return for faith, so you lose nothing of your worldly affairs by following them, and you hope with them for guidance in your religion.

﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.﴾ This is addressed to his people: listen to my words and act upon my counsel. It is said that it is addressed to the messengers, so that they may bear witness for him.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verses 28–29:

﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven﴾. The meaning is that God destroyed them with a single cry (ṣayḥa) that Jibril (Gabriel) let out, and He did not need to send down a host from the heaven to punish them, because they were too insignificant for that. It has also been said that the meaning is: God did not send down upon his people angels as messengers, as the Quraysh said: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him, so that he could be a warner with him?﴾ [al-Furqan: 7]. The word "host" (jund) is more fitting for the first meaning, and likewise the mention of the cry afterwards. ﴿And We never sent down [a host]﴾: that is, We were not going to send down a host from the heaven upon anyone. ﴿Then they were extinguished﴾: that is, they were still and motionless, neither moving nor speaking.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verse 30:

﴿Alas for the servants!﴾ It is an address to regret, as if he said: "O regret, come, for this is your time." This lamentation over them is a metaphor conveying the sense of magnifying and exalting the enormity of what they did by mocking the messengers. It may be that it is the speech of the angels or of the believers among mankind. It has also been said: the meaning is, "O regret of the servants over themselves."

﴿Did they not see﴾ The pronoun refers either to the Quraysh or to mankind in general, and the seeing here means knowing. ﴿And indeed all of them, all together, will be brought before Us﴾. It is read as "lamma" with light pronunciation, where the lam is the lam of emphasis entering upon the extra "ma", and "in" in this case is the light form of the heavy "inna". It is also read with the heavy pronunciation ("lammā"), where it means "illa" (except), and "in" in this case is a negation particle.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verse 77:

﴿Have not the human being seen that We created him from a drop of semen?﴾ This verse and what follows it to the end of the surah are proofs for the gathering (al-hashr) on the Day of Resurrection, and a refutation of those who deny that. The "nutfah" is the drop of semen (al-mani) from which the human being was created. There is no doubt that the God (al-Ilah) who was able to create the human being from a drop is able to create him again at the Resurrection (al-ba'th). The occasion of revelation of the verse: al-'As ibn Wa'il came to the Prophet ﷺ with a decayed bone and said: "O Muhammad, who will give life to this?" It is also said that the one who brought the bone was Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and it is also said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Allah will give it life, and will cause you to die, then will give you life, and will enter you into Hell." ﴿Then behold, he is an open adversary﴾, that is: a speaker, capable of disputation, who makes clear what is in his self by his tongue.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verses 78–79:

﴿And he presents for Us a parable﴾ refers to the saying of the disbelievers: "Who will give life to these bones?" ﴿and forgets his own creation﴾, meaning he forgets to reason from his original creation to his resurrection. The forgetting here may mean either heedlessness (dhuhul) or abandonment (tark). ﴿And they are decayed﴾, meaning worn away and crumbling. ﴿Say, "He will give them life who brought them into being the first time"﴾, which is reasoning from the first creation to the resurrection. ﴿And He is Knowledgeable of every creation﴾, meaning He knows how to create everything, so the resurrection of bodies after their annihilation is not difficult for Him. The word "creation" (khalq) here may be either a verbal noun (masdar) or in the sense of "what is created" (makhluq).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verse 80:

﴿Who has made for you fire from the green tree﴾ This is another proof of the possibility of resurrection. Those among the disbelievers and the naturalists (al-tabā'iyyūn) who denied it said: the nature of death is opposed to the nature of life, so how can bones become alive? So God established against them a proof from the green tree, full of water, even though the nature of water is opposed to the nature of fire. By "the tree" is meant the firestick of the Arabs (zinad), which is the tree of al-markh and al-, fār, for a green branch is cut from each of the two, dripping with water; then al-markh is rubbed against al-'afār and fire is struck between them. Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no tree but that there is fire in it, except the jujube (al-'unnāb), but it is more abundant in al-markh and al-'afār.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verses 81–82:

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ Yes! This is another proof for the resurrection: the God who was able to create the heavens and the earth, despite their magnitude and the vastness of their bodies, is able to create the bodies of the children of Adam after they have perished. The pronoun in "mithlahum" (their likes) refers to the people. ﴿And He is the All-Creator, the All-Knowing.﴾ Mention of these two names also serves as evidence for the resurrection, and likewise in His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ For this is an expression of His power over all things, and there is no doubt that the All-Creator, the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, does not find it difficult to restore the bodies.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 36, verse 83:

﴿So glory be to the One in whose hand is the dominion of everything﴾.
